headline: High: shared filesystem and MCP create default cross-agent injection, leakage, and write-conflict risks; compliance risk is lower but nontrivial.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Continue can read workspace files and use MCP, while MinerU accepts local document inputs and exposes an MCP server. That creates a plausible bridge where content from one agent can be fed into the other as trusted text. The shared filesystem path is documented for Continue, but the exact orchestration is not, so I choose medium over low.
conditions: IF Continue ingests MinerU-produced files from the shared workspace as instructions
IF an MCP server relays document text between the agents without provenance tagging
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of generated documents as prompts
Separate workspaces per agent
Require provenance labels on all inter-agent files
Restrict MCP servers to allowlisted tools only
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: Continue touches source code and open editor buffers and can write/read the filesystem; MinerU processes PDFs, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, JSON, and OCR text. In a shared workspace, either agent can expose sensitive file contents to the other’s processing path. MinerU is offline by default, which lowers blast radius, but the shared-file pathway still exists.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace directory
IF sensitive source code or documents are present in files readable by Continue and processed by MinerU
mitigations: Use separate directories per agent
Exclude secrets and private docs from shared folders
Turn off automatic file pickup in either agent
Review logs for accidental content capture
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls at the filesystem layer

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Continue has broad filesystem write plus shell/subprocess capability, and its shared state is via filesystem. MinerU also supports file inputs and concurrent inference, so both can mutate or consume the same workspace without documented locking. That matches the rubric’s dangerous shared-write pattern closely enough to rate high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or git checkout
IF one agent rewrites files while the other reads them concurrently
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories
Pause one agent before the other writes
Use file locks around shared artifacts
Avoid concurrent edits to the same repo
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Continue can generate code or edits from workspace context, and MinerU can extract structured text from documents. If MinerU output is fed into Continue without verification, Continue may act on extracted facts as authoritative. The pair is not inherently action-taking, so medium fits better than high, but the default file-based bridge still enables propagation of errors.
conditions: IF MinerU extraction results are pasted or saved into files that Continue treats as ground truth
IF Continue uses extracted tables or OCR text without human verification
mitigations: Require human review before acting on extracted text
Keep raw extraction outputs separate from task prompts
Add checksum or source-link fields to extracted records
Use a second-pass verifier for critical facts
requires-engineering: implement provenance-aware downstream validation

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are open-source and document-processing/coding tools with no explicit residency, HIPAA, or DPA claims in the profiles. The main compliance concern is that Continue handles model-provider API keys and broad workspace content, while MinerU is described as private/offline. Because no concrete mismatch is documented, this is a low-confidence, low-severity gap rather than a breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Continue and sent to a noncompliant model provider
IF organizational policy requires documented residency or retention guarantees that are absent here
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared workspaces
Use a compliant local model for Continue
Review provider retention settings
Document data-handling policy for both tools
requires-engineering: obtain vendor compliance attestations
